blocking: AMENDED 2026-09-20 ~00:4xZ by 1.0.0_SA_CTO. READ THIS PARAGRAPH BEFORE THE TEXT BELOW; it supersedes two sentences in it and adds a routing that was missing entirely. (A) RULED: LGIC_CANON IS **NOT** HELD AT STOP, AND THAT IS WHY THE /self-drive LGIC SCOPE IS NOT TERMINAL. LGIC_ENFORCE was held at round 19 and LGIC_LGCTFM at round 10, both on the test 'I name NO in-engine outcome a round could move'. THAT TEST DOES NOT PASS HERE. Step 13's own recorded reason -- quoted from THIS field and verified at the bytes rather than restated -- says the correction ALREADY LANDED in that cell's own commit, so its CARDED status is a VINTAGE ARTIFACT of the run rather than live work, and 'a re-run should read 13 REACHED + 3 CARDED, and confirming that is one cheap cell for the next round'. A confirmation cell IS an in-engine act. Measured by 2.0.0_SA_COO~G (98425), which holds this project's coo_lane, and VERIFIED AT THE BYTES BY THIS SEAT because the claim that keeps the loop running is the one this seat most benefits from inheriting. (B) THE ROUTING THAT WAS MISSING, AND IT IS THIS SEAT'S DEFECT: LGIC_ENFORCE's round-17 analysis stated that LGIC_CANON-W3-S2's l2_recount() defect 'is LGIC_CANON's, it is BLOCKING there, and this analysis routes it rather than absorbing it.' THAT ROUTING NEVER REACHED THIS CARRIER. Measured 2026-09-20: the row exists in this project's channel at class BLOCKING but hazard_standing INERT and disarm_owner None, and neither 'l2_recount' nor 'W3-S2' appeared anywhere in this register's phase or blocking. A ROUTING WITHOUT AN OWNER IS A FILING -- the same defect as 'a broker message is NEVER the carrier', one level up: a defect routed to another PROJECT by a sentence written in the ROUTING project's own analysis, where the destination's readers never meet it. ROUTED HERE NOW, WITH ITS CONTENT: check_canon_r2.py's l2_recount() parses ledger_recount.py's SECTION/TOTAL lines with single-token regexes and cannot read multi-word disposition-class labels, so L2-AC4 reads FAIL regardless of the ledger's true counts. It is a live quality defect of this project, and it is NOT a retirement -- LGIC_ENFORCE round 17 ruled LIVE is the correct class on this project's own one-round-old precedent, because classing a pending repair as RETIRED-* would launder it into a closure. (C) THE NEXT ROUND'S NATURAL SHAPE, stated as a finding and NOT as a cut, which is 2.0.0_SA_COO~G's under Rule 27: step 13's confirmation and the W3-S2 repair are the SAME ROUND's work, both cheap and both in-engine. (D) SUPERSEDED BELOW: this field states 'ADVI_FIRMBKTS reads status active, dep_stage PRD, coo_lane null -- UNSEATED'. THE COO_LANE HALF STILL HOLDS; THE GATE HALF DOES NOT. Measured now: python .tools/prd-signoff.py status ADVI_FIRMBKTS reads v1.3 @30d612d5e5 ADMITTED, ratified-text SIGNED by 3.0.0_SA_CVO CURRENT and brief SIGNED by 4.0.0_SA_CRO CURRENT (the brief half landed @2bcb0a340b, hours after the superseded sentence was written). THE CARRIER IS NOT WRONG, IT IS OLDER THAN THE FACT. So the L4-R gate between ADVI_FIRMBKTS and a seat HAS CLEARED and what remains is purely a SEATING decision -- the same shape this seat ruled FWD-5 clause 2 into at LGIC_ENFORCE: not blocked on a missing DECISION but on a missing SEAT. When that seating goes to Andrew it carries ADMITTED, never the older early-in-PRD framing. --- SUPERSEDED TEXT, RETAINED IN FULL (R-43): Not blocked on a document and not blocked on a seat. ROUND 4 is CLOSED at L10 with its L9 now graded (@ea61b36cbb, C6R4-AC8 PASS) and the channel at 48 items / 0 undispositioned. WHAT REMAINS IS FWD-5 AND IT IS NOT BOUGHT BY ANOTHER CELL: it closes when the firm's people can see their dashboard at the end of the checklist run, which is an act outside this project's engine -- the same shape as LGIC_LGCTFM's FWD-4 and FWD-6. The 4 carded steps name their owners and are the list of what stands between the run and that dashboard. ZERO OPEN ORDERS IS NOT DONE (R-51): DONE reads from the PRD's FWD outcome array plus `status` off `active`, and no `completion_test` field exists or is minted. A project with no open orders and an unrealized outcome is a project between rounds. L4-R remains ADMITTED at v1.7 -- brief half SIGNED by 2.0.0_SA_COO~O, ratified-text SIGNED by 3.0.0_SA_CVO, both current; `python .tools/prd-signoff.py status LGIC_CANON` is the one read. CONVERGENCE MEASURED 2026-09-18 ~17:2xZ by 1.0.0_SA_CTO at C6_RUN_RECORD.json's `carded` array, because "the 4 carded steps name their owners" did not say that TWO OF THEM ARE THE SAME OWNER AND THE SAME ACT: step 10 owner ADVI_FIRMBKTS (the edge auth validator and shared advisor router read tier-first platinum keys `platinum/{firmId}/ownership_map.json` and `platinum/advi/{firm}/` that address() cannot produce, until ADVI_FIRMBKTS's router repoint lands) and step 16 owner ADVI_FIRMBKTS ("same router repoint as Step 10") plus a live portal sign-in. SO 2 OF 4 CARDED STEPS ARE ONE ROOT CAUSE, NOT TWO ITEMS. Step 14 is Andrew's (SOVEREIGN portal-paths input, row LGIC_CANON-W6-S2) with 1.0.0_SA_CTO as co-owner for register entry X8 -- and the CTO half cannot move first, because which firm the X8 entry names depends on the portal-paths grant. Step 13's owner is LGIC_ENFORCE and its own recorded reason says the correction ALREADY LANDED IN THAT CELL'S OWN COMMIT, so its CARDED status is a VINTAGE ARTIFACT of the run rather than live work: a re-run should read 13 REACHED + 3 CARDED, and confirming that is one cheap cell for the next round rather than an assumption to carry. THE CROSS-PROJECT POINT, which neither project's carrier stated: ADVI_FIRMBKTS ALSO GATES LGIC_LGCTFM's FWD-6, whose ACCEPT names "the 49 Financial migration" verbatim at PRD :119-120. CORRECTED 2026-09-19 ~14:3xZ by 1.0.0_SA_CTO, AGAINST ITS OWN PRIOR SENTENCE, after PRINTING THE BYTES AT :115-124 RATHER THAN RESTATING THIS CARRIER: THE TWO OUTCOMES ARE GATED AT DIFFERENT DEPTHS AND THIS LINE READ AS THOUGH THEY WERE GATED AT THE SAME ONE. FWD-6's ACCEPT is "the 49 Financial migration's decomposition starts from the run's plan instead of rebuilding the inventory from scratch", DONE WHEN "EXERCISED -- a real migration's decomposition has been cut from it". That is an L5 act: it closes when a SEATED lane CUTS A DECOMPOSITION from the run's plan, and it does NOT wait for the router repoint or for any migration to execute. LGIC_CANON's FWD-5 is the deep one -- it needs the ADVI_FIRMBKTS ROUTER REPOINT TO LAND (steps 10 and 16), which is deep in that project's L7. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, WHICH THE OVERSTATEMENT HID: SEATING ADVI_FIRMBKTS CLOSES ONE LGIC OUTCOME ALMOST IMMEDIATELY AND THE OTHER MUCH LATER, so the seat buys more, and sooner, than "it gates two final outcomes" suggested. THE QUOTE AND THE LINE NUMBERS WERE CORRECT AND THE IMPLICATION WAS MINE -- an inherited universal with no denominator beside it to interrogate, which is this seat's named standing failure mode (CLAUDE.md Rule 24, the inherited-claim clause). ADVI_FIRMBKTS reads status active, dep_stage PRD, coo_lane null -- UNSEATED -- measured at its project.json this tick. So ONE UNSEATED PROJECT IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE FINAL OUTCOME OF TWO LGIC PROJECTS, and its seating is an open call at Andrew (CALL 2, surfaced 2026-09-18 ~08:4xZ). That reclassifies the seating question from a scheduling preference to the LGIC scope's critical path, and it is surfaced to him on that basis rather than re-asked.
